title: I Am Nujood, Age 10 and Divorced
author: Nujood Ali with Delphine Minoui
target_audience: General adult readers interested in memoirs
Readers concerned with human rights and child welfare
Students and professionals in gender studies, Middle Eastern studies, and social justice
Advocates for children’s and women’s rights
core_themes: Courage and resilience in the face of adversity
The power of individual action and advocacy
Legal and social barriers to justice for women and children
primary_purpose: To narrate the true story of Nujood Ali, a Yemeni girl who at age 10 escaped her forced marriage and secured a divorce, illuminating the brutal realities of child marriage and inspiring global awareness and advocacy for children’s rights.

structure_format.organization: Chronological memoir, beginning with Nujood’s life before marriage, the ordeal of her marriage, her escape, the court proceedings, and the aftermath
features: Insights into family, community, and cultural expectations
Details of legal struggle and courtroom experiences

key_concepts_lessons: Child marriage remains a present and critical human rights issue, particularly in some regions.
The courage of an individual, even a child, can challenge longstanding social norms and laws.
Support systems—such as family allies, lawyers, and journalists—are crucial in enabling change.
Legal intervention is possible for those facing injustice, though fraught with societal and legal barriers.
Telling one’s story can be a powerful catalyst for broader social change.
style_tone: Alternates between innocence and maturity born of hardship
Matter-of-fact reporting of painful and traumatic events
notable_features: Firsthand account of a landmark legal case for children’s rights in Yemen
Gained worldwide attention and became a symbol of the global fight against child marriage
Includes contextual information on customs and laws in Yemen
Short, accessible narrative suitable for a wide readership
cultural_historical_context: Set in early 21st-century Yemen, where arranged and child marriages are still practiced. Nujood’s case became a catalyst for debate and reform on children’s and women’s rights in Yemen and inspired global advocacy against child marriage.
reception_impact: Helped spark global conversations about child marriage
Nujood was named one of Glamour’s Women of the Year in 2008
Lauded for its bravery—though some critics note the story’s simplicity or the challenges Nujood continued to face after the events described
comparable_titles: A House Without Windows by Nadia Hashimi
Half the Sky by Nicholas D. Kristof and Sheryl WuDunn
